newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan stocks close higher, led by blue chips.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan stocks close higher, led by blue chips.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed higher on Friday on foreign buying of blue chips, brokers sid.
The all share index rose 1.23 points to 562.03, largely thanks to a 4.25-rupee rise by blue chip JKH to 171.25 rupees.
"You have to pay a premium to get shares in bulk," said Gordon Nadesan of brokerage CT Smith. "The premium (for JKH) was not too steep."

Distilleries Co of Sri Lanka bought a 51 percent stake in Balangoda Plantations being privatised by Colombo at 420.75 million rupees. It was the highest price for a controlling stake in a plantation firm ever sold by the government.
The previous high for a controlling stake in a plantation firm was 359.55 million rupees recorded on August 23 for Agarapatana Plantations.
Brokers said many institutions focused their attention to the outcome of the Balangoda Plantations tender.
Friday's turnover was a moderate 13.15 million rupees on 245,304 shares. Brokers said foreign investors bought 50,000 JKH shares.
